players.name: Matt Short
players.bio:
A highly-talented allrounder, Matt Short played for Australia in the 2014 Under-19 World Cup where he impressed with 237 runs.

The off-spinner from Northcote made his debut for Victoria at the start of the 2014-15 summer, but he would briefly trade his allegiance in the competition to the Cricket Australia XI, where he was vice-captain in the 2016 One-Day Cup.

Beginning his Big Bash career at the Melbourne Renegades, it took a move to the Adelaide Strikers to find his feet in the competition, named player of the tournament in consecutive seasons in KFC BBL|12 and BBL|13.

It was around this time he was also hitting top form in the Sheffield Shield for Victoria, blasting a career-best 623 runs in the 2022-23 season to go with 10 wickets at 21.50.

In 2023 Short made his international debut in both ODIs and T20s after touring with the side in South Africa and India.

players.name: Alex Carey
players.didyouKnow: Alex Carey was captain of the Greater Western Sydney Giants in 2010, prior to them joining the AFL.
players.bio:
After starting out as a cricketer, Carey decided to pursue a career in Australian Rules football and as an 18-year-old was the inaugural captain and Best and Fairest Award winner for the newly formed Greater Western Sydney Giants in his first season. But Carey was axed by the club as they prepared to enter the top tier AFL competition in 2012, and was soon lured back to cricket by the South Australian Redbacks. There has been no looking back ever since.

Carey had long been highly regarded by South Australia, having played under-age cricket for the state.

Having returned to the state set-up he soon switched from full-time batter to wicketkeeper-batter and found form, taking the gloves full-time for the state in the 2015-16 summer.

The left-hander played a big role in securing Adelaide Strikers' BBL|07 title win in 2017-18 – his incredible ton against the Hobart Hurricanes being a standout performance, and had narrowly missed out on Test selection for that summer's Ashes series. But his terrific run of form earned him his ODI & T20I debuts early in 2018, with the wicketkeeper soon donning the role of vice-captain in both formats, including at the 2019 ODI World Cup in England where he epitomised Aussie grit to bat on, bloodied and bandaged, after being struck on the chin during the semi-final.

His Test call up came in the 2021-22 summer to replace Tim Paine as Australia's gloveman, receiving Baggy Green cap No.461 from Adam Gilchrist at the Gabba, with a maiden ton coming following summer at the Boxing Day Test against South Africa.

In a battle with Josh Inglis for the role of gloveman for Australia's white-ball teams, Carey remained a mainstay of the Test team. He famously stumped Jonny Bairstow during the 2023 Ashes Test at Lord's when the Englishman wandered out of his crease off the bowling of Cameron Green.

In a purple patch with the bat throughout the 2024-25 summer and beyond, Carey scored a century in the Sheffield Shield final as South Australia broke their title drought in March 2025.

players.name: Josh Inglis
players.bio:
England-born but WA-bred, Josh Inglis made his first-class debut for the Cricket Australia XI in 2015 in a tour match against West Indies.

The versatile wicketkeeper-batter was rewarded with a Western Australia contract at the beginning of the 2016-17 season, but it wasn't until the 2019-20 summer that Inglis started to really make his mark.

That Big Bash campaign the right-hander finished with 405 runs (just 20 runs behind Scorchers' leading run-scorer Liam Livingstone), including four half-centuries.

The next year, in BBL|10, he exceeded the 400-run barrier again and followed up with some impressive performances for London Spirit in the inaugural season of The Hundred.

By this stage, Inglis was firmly in the eyes of the Australian selectors and in February 2022 he made his international debut in a home T20 against Sri Lanka before an ODI debut – this time away to Sri Lanka – followed in June of the same year.

At the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, for which Inglis was selected as the squad's reserve keeper, he replaced Alex Carey in the XI after one match and held his spot throughout for Australia's famous victory in Ahmedabad.

During Australia's tour of the United Kingdom in 2024, Inglis set a new Australian record with a 43-ball T20 century against Scotland.

He became Australia's 30th ODI captain, and the 14th in T20 internationals, when named to lead in home series against Pakistan in 2024-25, while his hot form also earned him a maiden call up to the Test squad as a specialist batter for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy series.

He made his Test debut against Sri Lanka in Galle in late January 2025, scoring a century on debut, making him only the fourth Australian man to score centuries in all three formats of the game.

players.name: Marnus Labuschagne
players.didyouKnow: Labuschagne was part of Queensland's triumphant Sheffield Shield side in 2017/18, finishing the season as the competition's second-highest run-scorer
players.bio:
Born in South Africa, Marnus Labuschagne migrated with his family to Brisbane in 2004 and entered the Queensland Cricket underage system when he was 11.

The top-order batter made his first-class debut in the opening round of the 2014–15 Sheffield Shield campaign, aged 20, grinding out 83 runs against South Australia as an opener.

With just three List A games under his belt heading into the 2016-17 season, Labuschagne turned heads by being named Player of the Tournament for the 2016 Matador One-Day Cup, finishing with 273 runs at 45 to help steer the Bulls into the final.

The following season Labuschagne hit his straps in the red-ball arena, featuring in Queensland's triumphant Sheffield Shield side, and finishing the season as the competition's second-highest run-scorer with 795 runs at 39.75, including two hundreds.

Several months later, Labuschagne was awarded with Test cap No.455 on Australia's tour of the UAE in October 2018, making 0 and 13 on debut.

After losing and then regaining his spot in the following home summer, the right-hander's Test career really took off in 2019 when after an unexpected Ashes cameo (becoming Test cricket's first concussion substitute, replacing Steve Smith at Lord's) he ended up being the world's leading run-scorer in Tests for the calendar year. What followed was a dominant home season which included four centuries from five matches, including a double-century.

Arguably one of Labuschagne's best centuries came during the 2023 Ashes series, when the Queenslander held off a rampant England attack to score an invaluable 111 in Manchester, securing the draw that would retain the urn.

Labuschagne was initially left out of Australia's 15-man squad for the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, but an injury to Ashton Agar opened the door for the middle-order batter and he took it with both hands, playing every match of Australia's campaign and scoring a crucial 58 not out in the final.

The prolific batter played his 50th Test match in New Zealand in March 2024 with over 4,000 runs to his name in the format, having established himself as Australia's No.3 since that breakout Ashes campaign in 2019.

Form deserted him in 2024-25 and, after a makeshift stint as opener in Australia's 2025 World Test Championship Final defeat to South Africa, he was dropped from the Test side for the West Indies tour.

players.name: Cameron Green
players.bio:
Cameron Green had no shortage of hype to live up to in the early stages of his career having been touted as an international-calibre player since his early teens.

The towering allrounder, who stands nearly two metres tall, burst onto the first-class scene as a 17-year-old in February 2017 when he took a five-wicket haul against Tasmania in his first Sheffield Shield appearance with Western Australia.

His first 30 first-class wickets came at an average of just 22.53 but as stress fractures in his back limited his bowling in the ensuing years, it was the strides he made with the bat that vaulted him into national calculations.

Green's breakout game came in November 2019 when he hit unbeaten scores of 87 and 121 from No.8 and 9 against Queensland, which saw him promoted up the WA order and subsequently flourish as a top-order player with two more centuries in the season, before 197 off 438 against NSW in October 2020.

A mainstay in WA's top four and having resumed bowling following months of remedial work on his action, he earned a call-up to Australian squads in late 2020, making his ODI and Test debut that summer against India.

He passed fifty in five of his first six series, took a maiden five-wicket haul at the MCG against South Africa in the 2022 Boxing Day Test, and hit his first Test century against India in Ahmedabad in March 2023, all while building a stunning highlight reel of remarkable catches in the gully.

Opening the batting on a T20I tour of India in September 2022 proved life-changing, flaying a pair of impressive fifties that led to him being bought for a then-record A$3.15million by Mumbai Indians in that year's IPL auction, and rewarded his purchasers with a 47-ball century that elevated them into the playoffs.

A hamstring issue in the 2023 Ashes saw him lose his spot to fellow WA allrounder Mitch Marsh but, so eager were selectors to get him back into the side, Steve Smith was moved up to open the batting in the wake of David Warner's Test retirement to accommodate Green at No. 4. He struck a masterful unbeaten 174 not out in his new role against New Zealand in Wellington in February 2024.

After developing a stress fracture in his back in mid-2024 Green opted for surgery that ruled him out for that summer's Border-Gavaskar Trophy series and restricted him from bowling until late in 2025. He returned as a batter only via the UK's County Championship in mid-2025 playing as a No.3. After building up bowling loads in the Sheffield Shield, Green was shown the confidence to be named as an allrounder in Australia's squad for the opening Ashes Test that summer.

players.name: Matt Renshaw
players.didyouKnow: In December 2018, Renshaw scored 345 for Toombul off 273 balls, with 38 fours and 12 sixes, a record for Brisbane senior cricket.
players.bio:
An Under-19 representative for Australia, Renshaw burst onto the domestic scene in December 2015 when struck an epic 170 against a strong NSW attack to become the youngest first-class century maker for Queensland. Born in Yorkshire, he was a family friend of England batter Joe Root as a youngster.

After his mammoth breakout innings, Renshaw finished his maiden Sheffield Shield campaign as Queensland's leading Shield run scorer with 738 at 43.41 in 2015-16.

In 2017, Renshaw became the first Australian cricketer to make 500 Test runs before turning 21 years old which included a memorable 184 against Pakistan in Sydney.

However, following his dream start a difficult six Tests in Asia (four in India, two in Bangladesh) and a barren start to the following Shield season saw Renshaw left out of the Aussie team for the 2017-18 Ashes series, with Cameron Bancroft preferred.

Ironically, it was Renshaw who was called up to replace the suspended Bancroft during the ill-fated tour of South Africa in early 2018.

A couple of lean seasons saw Renshaw move to the middle order, where he flourished during the Covid-affected 2020-21 summer, scoring 500 Shield runs at an average of 62.50. His one-day and T20 form also improved following his positional shift.

A strong county campaign with Somerset in 2022 followed and ahead of the 2022-23 New Year's Test against South Africa, Renshaw was recalled to the Australian XI.

The tall left-hander also played two Tests on Australia's unsuccessful tour to India in 2023.

Two centuries for Australia A as opener saw him return to the top of the order for the 2023-24 Marsh Sheffield Shield season and 2024 County Championship season.

players.name: Ollie Peake
players.bio:
The left-handed batter from Geelong has been a star on the rise ever since he burst onto the scene during the 2024 U19 World Cup, when he came into Australia's squad as a 17-year-old.

A late arrival to South Africa as an injury replacement, Peake was brought straight into the playing XI and made an immediate impact with 25 not out against England in his first match, a crucial 49 against Pakistan in the semi-final and 46no against India in Australia's win in the final.

Having impressed with a half-century on his Sheffield Shield debut for Victoria in 2024-25, he was invited to join Australia's Test squad for a taste of the top level in early 2025 on a Sri Lanka tour. He earned his first full contracts with Victoria and the Melbourne Renegades for the 2025-26 summer, and was drafted into the Australia A side.

He made headlines by hitting a last-ball six to win a BBL match in Perth, then went directly from the stadium to the airport to return to the U19 World Cup – now in Namibia and Zimbabwe in early 2026 – this time as Australia's captain, emulating his father Clinton Peake, who had captained Australia U19s in 1994-95.

His first official call-up to a senior Australia side came in winter 2026 when he was named in the ODI side to play three matches in Pakistan, making his debut in the first match in Rawalpindi batting in the lower middle order.

At 19 years and 261 days he was officially Australia's youngest ever specialist batter to make his ODI debut, beating the record of Ricky Ponting (20 years and 58 days).

players.name: Nathan Ellis
players.bio:
From a labourer struggling to make ends meet to an international cricketer, the journey of Nathan Ellis is one of extraordinary dedication and persistence.

Raised in Sydney, Ellis relocated to Hobart in 2017 in search of an opportunity at the next level having dominated NSW Premier Cricket by taking 160 wickets at 22 in four seasons.

A consistent contributor for the Hobart Hurricanes since his debut in 2018, the right-armer quickly became one of the competition's best death bowlers with twin weapons of an excellent change of pace and pinpoint yorkers.

On the shorter side for a quick, making his deliveries skid on, he has earned multiple stints in overseas T20 leagues where he has impressed for Hampshire (T20 Blast), London Spirit (Hundred) and Punjab Kings (IPL).

He made an instant impact on T20 international debut for Australia with a hat-trick against Bangladesh in 2021, also earning an ODI cap in Pakistan in 2022. With opportunities to represent Australia limited behind a generational pool of talent, Ellis initially had to bide his time, called up for his first World Cup role at the 2024 T20 event in the Caribbean.

While he has also enjoyed success with the red-ball at first-class level after making his debut for Tasmania in 2020, his overseas and international opportunities have come exclusively in the white-ball formats, helping him earn a Cricket Australia contract for 2024-25 after being upgraded during the previous season.

Ellis was appointed Hurricanes captain ahead of BBL|13, replacing Matthew Wade, and captained the side to the BBL|14 title in January 2025.

players.name: Tanveer Sangha
players.bio:
Ever since a 16-year-old Tanveer Sangha caught the eye of former Australia spinner Fawad Ahmed in 2018, the young leggie has been one to watch.

The son of Indian migrants in Sydney’s south-west suburbs, Sangha started his junior cricket career as a fast bowler and it wasn’t until his early teens – when he discovered his skill as a leg-spinner – that his passion for the game started to develop.

Having made an instant impact in club cricket, he was quickly ushered into under-age teams at state and international level, meeting Fawad during a series for Australia’s Under-16 team in Melbourne and then starring at the 2020 Under-19 World Cup in South Africa.

Later that year, having earned a rookie contract with the NSW Blues at the age of 18, Sangha made an instant impression in his debut season with the Sydney Thunder in the KFC BBL, displaying an excellent temperament and taking the wickets of some of the best players in the competition.

His New South Wales debuts followed, earning his first caps in the Marsh Sheffield Shield and Marsh Cup at the start of the 2021-22 summer.

Australia's tours to South Africa and India in 2023 proved to be a valuable experience for the fledgling spinner, making his ODI and T20 international debuts for the national side and being the sole 'travelling reserve' for the Aussie squad during their successful ODI World Cup campaign.

players.name: Matt Kuhnemann
players.bio:
A left-arm spinner from the Gold Coast, Matthew Kuhnemann was handed a rookie contact by Queensland for 2016-17.

He is a former Australia Under-19 player and toured Sri Lanka in 2014, while he played for the Cricket Australia XI during their time in the domestic one-day competition.

He rose to prominence however in 2019 for the Brisbane Heat, taking two wickets on his BBL debut.

He impressed for the Heat over the proceeding seasons and was a crucial member of their BBL|13 championship as their most economical bowler along with 10 wickets for the season.

He earnt a Sheffield Shield debut with Queensland in February 2021, then in 2022, Kuhnemann was called up to the Australian ODI squad for their tour of Sri Lanka, taking six wickets in his four matches during the tour, putting himself in the frame for selection on future tours of the subcontinent in both white- and red-ball cricket.

That opportunity came a year later in India when he was parachuted from a Shield game at the MCG to make his Test debut in the second Border-Gavaskar match in Delhi. He retained his spot for the rest of the series, collecting a five-wicket haul in the third Test in Indore to help Australia to a nine-wicket victory.

But his red-ball opportunities for Queensland dried up in 2023-24 when leg-spinner Mitchell Swepson was preferred, with Kuhnemann signing a three-year deal to join Tasmania ahead of the 2024-25 season.

In July 2025, Kuhnemann made his T20I debut during Australia's Caribbean tour.

players.name: Adam Zampa
players.didyouKnow: Zampa was the leading wicket-taker for Australia in the 2016 ICC World Twenty20 hosted by India.
players.bio:
A leg-spinner from New South Wales' south coast, Adam Zampa showed early signs of his ability after playing an instrumental role in Australia's successful campaign at the 2010 Under-19 World Cup.

Following his impressive performances for South Australia and the Melbourne Stars, the wily spinner made his way into Australia's ODI and T20I squads in 2016. Zampa emerged as Australia's leading wicket-taker at the T20 World Cup hosted by India the same year.

By 2019 Zampa had established himself as one of the first picked bowlers in Australia's ODI and T20 setups, and an impressive career trajectory has seemingly seen him improve year-on-year.

Typifying the modern white-ball wrist spinner with a skidding stock delivery, Zampa proved crucial in Australia's maiden T20 World Cup triumph in the UAE in 2021.

He finished with 13 wickets at an economy rate of just 5.81 and was considered by several judges as unlucky not to be named Player of the Tournament.

He again played a vital role in Australia's 2023 ODI World Cup victory, overcoming a slow start to finish the tournament as the second highest wicket-taker with 23.

He became the first Australian bowler to play 100 T20 Internationals during the Carribean tour in mid-2025

players.name: Maaz Sadaqat
players.bio:
A hard-hitting left-hand batter top-order batter and left-arm orthodox spinnner, Maaz Sadaqat arrived on the international scene in early 2026 in the 50-over format.

A breakout performance at the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in 2025, where he was the top run scorer, led to an international debut against Bangladesh in March 2026, and he was retained for their home ODI series against Australia.

players.name: Arafat Minhas
players.bio: Arafat Minhas made a memorable ODI debut against Australia, taking a match-winning five-wicket haul in Rawalpindi to become the first Pakistani to claim a five-for on debut. A left-arm finger spinner, Minhas produced a sensational six-ball burst that removed Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne and Cameron Green, the latter two without scoring.
